1.why: UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing across cards and forms.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case without italics or all-caps, and text is broken into short paragraphs rather than dense blocks.

3.why: Layouts are single-column cards with large inputs and buttons that remain readable and usable at mobile widths.

4.why: Most instructions are brief plain-language sentences such as 'Store these now. They will not be shown again.'

5.why: Recovery-code fields show a formatted placeholder (ABCD-EFGH-JKLM) but many other inputs lack concrete examples of expected format.

6.why: No step forces the user to read a long block of text; content is limited to short headings, one-sentence help, and lists.

7.why: Setup key and recovery codes are displayed as plain text without a copy button or other one-click copy control.

8.why: Authenticator setup shows only a manual setup key and otpauth URI; no QR code or equivalent scannable alternative is offered.

9.why: Standard email/password fields are present and pre-filled, so browsers/password managers can interact, but no explicit autocomplete attributes or affordances are visible.

10.why: Page titles and primary blue buttons clearly indicate the current step and main action on each screen.

11.why: Each screen focuses on a single primary task (sign in, verify, save codes, etc.) with one main call-to-action.

12.why: After actions the UI shows clear status banners (e.g., 'MFA is active', 'Recovery code accepted', 'You are signed out') and next-step controls.

13.why: Users can regenerate recovery codes, retry verification, and navigate back without account penalties beyond normal lockout after repeated failures.

14.why: Error text such as 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' is non-blaming but does not explain the specific problem or concrete fix.

15.why: No reading time limits are imposed, yet the TOTP changes every 30 seconds and five failed attempts lock verification for five minutes, constraining entry time.
